subject: Delegated infra SLA letter / private deployment exception request
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@tidewell.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Leila Gomez <legal@tidewell.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment SLA exception – network ownership and uptime

Hannah,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. As we move to finalize our Private deployment, our legal and ops teams have flagged the SLA language around customer-controlled network and on-prem components.

Specifically, we need a short amendment confirming Redwood's operational commitments for the control plane and a clear statement of which latency/uptime obligations we can expect when the customer is operating the edge network and NATs.

High level asks:
- Control plane availability target (control-plane API endpoints used by the agent) — can Redwood commit to a 99.5% monthly uptime for the control plane even with customer peering?
- Latency SLO definition when the customer manages edge routing (we see spikes due to our transit provider; how will attribution work?)
- Evidence / observability: what telemetry you will provide to demonstrate your portion of the path is meeting SLOs (traces, synthetic checks, logs)

I'll attach our network diagram for context. If you can provide a short proposed addendum we can run it through legal.

Appreciate it,

Samir
Ops Lead | Tidewell Therapeutics
samir@tidewell.ai

Attachment: tidewell-network-diagram.png

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@tidewell.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jul 2028 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA exception – network ownership and uptime

Samir —

Thanks for the clear note and the diagram. I reviewed with Karthik (product) and Soojin (platform ops). We've drafted a focused addendum that attempts to split responsibilities while offering a limited, measurable commitment on Redwood's side. Key points in our proposed addendum (attached):

- Control plane uptime: Redwood proposes 99.5% monthly availability for the control plane endpoints that we operate (auth, roster, control API). This excludes customer-managed transit, peering, and NAT appliances.
- Latency SLO: For private/VPC deployments where customer edge is in-path, Redwood will commit to 95th percentile request-to-response latency for control-plane calls originating inside Redwood's region boundary. We will exclude tail latency attributable to customer-managed network elements identified in your diagram.
- Attribution & evidence: Redwood will provide:
  - Synthetic health checks from our edge points (results shared daily)
  - Per-request trace ids for a 30-day rolling window (redacted where needed) and tokenized cost/latency breakdowns
  - Monthly uptime report and incident root-cause write-ups when Redwood-side issues exceed thresholds

I've attached redwood-proposed-addendum-v1.pdf — this is intentionally short so your legal can quickly scan. If you can indicate which portions of the path Tidewell regards as 'in-scope' for network responsibility (e.g., transit provider, MPLS, NAT), we can mark them explicitly in the addendum.

CC'ing Karthik and Soojin to keep operations and product looped. Next steps: please review, propose any edits, and we can aim to iterate over DocuSign once both sides sign off.

Best,

Hannah Schmitt
Head, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood-proposed-addendum-v1.pdf

From: Samir Patel <samir@tidewell.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Leila Gomez <legal@tidewell.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Jul 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA exception – network ownership and uptime

Hannah,

Thanks — the addendum looks promising. A few clarifying questions from our side:

1) Can Redwood confirm the monitoring endpoints you will expose for synthetic checks and whether they will be accessible from our monitoring AD account? We prefer to pull the results into our dashboard rather than rely solely on emailed reports.

2) On the 99.5% control plane uptime: legal would like to see an explicit definition of "availability" (e.g., HTTP 200 response to health-check endpoint within 2s). Can you add that definition to the addendum? Also, we'd prefer a 99.7% target if feasible given our patient-facing SLAs — is there any flexibility?

3) Liability / credits: we expect a small SLA credit table if Redwood misses the committed availability. Can you propose sample credit language (we can negotiate numbers)

We attached our annotated diagram which highlights the customer-managed elements.

Thanks,
Samir
Attachment: tidewell-network-diagram-annotated.png

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@tidewell.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jul 2028 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA exception – network ownership and uptime

Samir — thanks for the follow-ups and the annotated diagram. Quick internal call with infra/legal folks this afternoon; here's what we can offer as a near-final approach (we'll formalize in v1.1 of the addendum):

- Availability definition: "Availability" = successful HTTP 200 from /healthz within 2s from Redwood's control-plane egress points. We will include the exact endpoint and health-check spec in v1.1.
- Uptime target: Redwood can accept 99.5% as a baseline for the control plane. For 99.7%, we can offer that as a customer-paid premium (we can include pricing for a 99.7% SLO upgrade in the addendum). This keeps the core commitment predictable while giving Tidewell an upgrade path.
- Monitoring access: we'll publish a read-only token to Tidewell's monitoring account for synthetic check results and maintain a 90-day rolling export. We'll also provide a short API (tokenized) to pull per-request latencies.
- Credits: propose a scaled credits table tied to monthly availability bands (example in the addendum). We'll include a clause that credits are the exclusive remedy for SLA failures.

I'll push the v1.1 addendum to the SUP-9123 ticket and share a DocuSign link once Tidewell confirms the wording. If Leila wants to loop in Redwood legal, happy to set up a short call.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

Related: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-9123
